cover.headline: Order, made visible.
cover.descriptor: Consulting and engineering for Africa's institutions.

pov.title: Our point of view
paragraphs: Every institution has a picture of how it is meant to run, and a way it really runs. The gap between the two is where the cost sits.
We close that gap in two moves. First we make the order: how money, people, operations and risk should flow. Then we make it visible: the system that shows, every day, whether they do.

system.title: What we build
system.lead: One system, assembled from parts that already fit each other.

pillars.title: A single record
pillars.body: One place where each number is produced, and one definition of what it means.

pillars.title: Work that moves
pillars.body: Approvals, hand-offs and deadlines that run on their own, and say when they do not.

pillars.title: An answer on demand
pillars.body: A question asked in plain language, answered from the institution's own data.

problems.title: Problems we answer
problems.lead: A selection, not a list. If yours is not here, it is the kind of thing we take on.

items.problem: The month-end is rebuilt by hand every month.
items.answer: We build the close once, and run it on a schedule anyone can see.

items.problem: Two reports disagree and nobody can say which is right.
items.answer: We settle the definitions, then make one of them the source.

items.problem: An approval lives in one person's inbox.
items.answer: We put the rule in the system, with a record of who decided what, and when.

problems.closing: The set is open. Bring us the one that costs you most.

method.title: How we work
method.lead: Four stages. Nothing is built before it is understood.

stages.name: See
stages.body: We map how the institution really runs today, from its own records, not from its chart.

stages.name: Design
stages.body: We agree how it should run, and write it down in words the people doing the work recognise.

stages.name: Build
stages.body: We build it in pieces that each stand on their own, and are in use before the next one starts.

stages.name: Hold
stages.body: We stay on it: the system is watched, improved and handed over properly.

principles.title: Foundation and floors
principles.body: The foundation is laid once and carries everything after it. Floors go up one at a time.

principles.title: Continuous improvement
principles.body: A system that is finished starts dying. Ours get a little better every month.

principles.title: Ownership
principles.body: The institution owns what we build: the code, the data and the knowledge to run it.

teams.title: Who does the work
teams.lead: Teams are described by discipline and credentials. We do not put names in a profile.

work.title: Work
work.lead: A few engagements, described as our clients allow.

items.client: A leading pharmaceutical manufacturer, with Tales Consulting
items.title: A close that runs itself
items.problem: The month-end was rebuilt by hand, and the board saw the numbers late.
items.built: One record for the close, with the steps scheduled and the exceptions raised as they happen.
items.outcome: The close now lands on a date the board can plan around.

items.title: One view of the depots
items.problem: Stock and sales were counted differently in every depot.
items.built: A single record of stock and sales, with the daily position visible to the head office.
items.outcome: Head office sees the same numbers the depots do, on the same day.

items.title: Your data stays yours
items.body: We work inside your systems where we can, and hand back everything we hold at the end.

items.title: Access is named
items.body: Every person who touches your data is named, and their access ends when the work does.

items.title: Written down
items.body: Confidentiality, retention and hand-back are in the engagement letter, not in a conversation.

contact.cta: Tell us the one thing that costs you most. We will tell you what it would take to fix it.
